title: perf-incident-postmortem-hotfix-validation
content:
Summary:

On 2026-02-25 we experienced degraded inference latency for a subset of hosted API traffic which caused an SLO miss for p99 token generation latency and triggered a customer escalation (CS-TICKET-8765). The degradation affected workloads with long sequence lengths (>512) and heavy prefix reuse patterns. The incident window lasted ~3 hours for impacted customers before a hotfix was rolled out; full remediation and validation completed the following day.

Impact:
- Scope: ~7% of production requests (by tail sequence-length distribution) routed to the hosted API during the window.
- Customer impact: 2 paying customers reported increased p99 latency and higher tail variance. One opened an escalation (CS-TICKET-8765).
- SLOs: p99 token latency SLO (<=150ms) was breached for the affected route between 2026-02-25T09:12 and 2026-02-25T12:20 UTC.
- Observable metrics (aggregated for affected route):
  - Baseline p50/p95/p99 (Feb 24): 22ms / 48ms / 82ms
  - During incident p50/p95/p99: 30ms / 120ms / 320ms
  - GPU utilization on impacted hosts rose from typical 68% to 94% (sustained)
  - CPU-side kernel scheduler saw 3x increase in kernel launch latency for attention kernels

Timeline (UTC):
- 2026-02-25 08:50 — Alert: automated SLO monitoring flagged elevated p99 for route "text-gen-long-prefix" (alert INF-SLO-02). Pager duty triggered.
- 2026-02-25 08:55 — On-call (Lucas) begins initial triage; confirms p99 spike and correlates with increased GPU queueing.
- 2026-02-25 09:05 — Customer success escalates via CS-TICKET-8765; customer reports timeouts and degraded UX.
- 2026-02-25 09:20 — Engineering (eng-serving-runtime) begins profiling on a replica of impacted host using nvprof / nsight and custom RPC tracing.
- 2026-02-25 10:10 — Profiling artifacts uploaded to S3 and basic analysis completed: attention kernel fallback observed for sequences >512 causing scalar fallback path with significantly slower execution; KV cache eviction rate increased by 2.2x.
- 2026-02-25 10:40 — Root cause hypothesis narrowed to a recent kernel-selection change in commit c3f5a (merged 2026-02-23) that altered kernel thresholds for fused attention -> fallback for specific sequence/block sizes.
- 2026-02-25 11:10 — Hotfix prepared: revert kernel-selection change and force-enable previously-performing fused-attention kernel for seq_len > 256 for GPU model family A100-80GB.
- 2026-02-25 11:35 — Hotfix deployed to 10% canary of impacted hosts; quick checks show p99 improvement.
- 2026-02-25 11:55 — Rollout increased to 100% for affected pool. Monitoring shows p99 returning to baseline by 12:20.
- 2026-02-26 09:00 — Extended validation and benchmark runs completed; permanent fix PR opened (PR #389).

Root cause:
- Immediate cause: A kernel-selection heuristic change (commit c3f5a) intended to improve memory usage for small-batch scenarios caused fused-attention to be skipped for common block sizes in long-seq workloads. This led to fallback to a slower reference kernel path that increased per-token compute time and created GPU scheduling contention.
- Contributing factors:
  - Incomplete coverage in our performance regression suite: sequence-length distribution used by CI did not include representative longer-prefix workloads or prefix-reuse patterns.
  - Canary cohort size and rollout gating did not exercise the long-seq traffic distribution present in some customers' workloads.
  - Monitoring thresholds were tuned for overall traffic; the route-level SLO alerting existed but defaulted to longer evaluation windows which delayed detection for this specific workload.

Investigation details (profiling & benchmarks):
- Tools used: nvprof, Nsight Systems, our RPC trace collector, kernel launch histograms, and perf microbench harness (bench/sequence-stress.py).
- Profiling findings:
  - Attention kernel launch latency histogram showed a secondary mode at ~3.6ms (fallback kernels) vs primary fused kernel mode at ~0.28ms.
  - KV cache churn: eviction rate increased from 0.9% to 2.0% for long-prefix requests due to longer per-request times and reduced throughput. This increased memory pressure and contributed to fallback behaviors in memory-constrained scenarios.
  - End-to-end traces showed token generation step dominated by attention kernel time during incident window (55% of per-token time vs baseline 18%).
- Benchmarks run for validation (selected results):
  - bench/sequence-stress.py --model redwood-open-7B --seq 1024 --batch 1 --iters 50
    - Baseline (pre-change) p99 token latency: 85ms
    - Regressed (with commit c3f5a) p99 token latency: 322ms
    - Hotfix (revert kernel selection): p99 token latency: 90ms
  - Throughput microbench (long-prefix mix): throughput drop of ~3.4x in regressed vs baseline; restored after hotfix.

Hotfix & validation steps applied:
1) Emergency revert: Reverted the specific kernel-selection threshold change (revert commit c3f5a) and added a short-circuit to prefer fused-attention for seq_len > 256 on A100 family. (Deployed 2026-02-25 11:35 UTC)
2) Canary rollout: 10% -> 100% over 20 minutes with continuous SLO monitoring.
3) Live validation: Ran focused perf tests against canary hosts (bench/sequence-stress) and compared Grafana traces for p50/p95/p99 pre/post.
4) Post-deploy stability run: 6-hour soak on impacted pool to ensure no regressions in other dimensions (memory, OOMs, CUDA errors).
5) Customer communication: CS notified affected customers of the mitigation and provided timeline & follow-up.

Validation results (post-hotfix):
- Grafana aggregated metrics for route: p99 returned to 80–95ms within ~45 minutes of full rollout.
- GPU utilization returned to normal ranges (60–75%); kernel launch histogram reverted to a single low-latency mode.
- No increase in OOMs or CUDA driver errors observed during soak.

Root-cause fix and long-term mitigations:
1) Permanent fix: PR #389 updates the kernel-selection logic to include an explicit safety whitelist for fused-attention on known-good family/seq_len combinations and provides a feature-flag to experiment at runtime. PR links in linked_artifacts.
2) Expand perf regression suite: add synthetic workloads that mimic long-prefix + prefix-reuse patterns; include sequences 512, 768, 1024 in CI perf tests. (Owner: Priya Nambiar, ETA: 2026-03-15)
3) Canary & rollout improvements: require that canary traffic includes stratified samples of long-seq-heavy customers for any runtime kernel/selection change. Update rollout gating to automagically throttle on route-level SLO deltas. (Owner: Lucas Patel, ETA: 2026-03-08)
4) Monitoring & alerting: add a faster-evaluating route-level SLO alert for p99 with shorter evaluation windows for routes tagged as "long-prefix". (Owner: Maya Chen, ETA: 2026-03-03)
5) Add kernel-level unit tests and microbench asserts to catch >2x regressions for known kernels when sequence lengths >512. (Owner: Ethan Brooks, ETA: 2026-03-10)
6) Postmortem blameless retrospective: scheduled 2026-03-02 16:00 UTC with eng-serving-runtime, product-hosted-api, and CS.

Action items (short list):
- [ ] Merge PR #389 after review and coordinate staged rollout with product (Owner: Maya Chen, due 2026-03-02)
- [ ] Add long-seq scenarios to CI perf suite (Owner: Priya Nambiar, due 2026-03-15)
- [ ] Implement canary sampling improvements (Owner: Lucas Patel, due 2026-03-08)
- [ ] Add route-level fast SLO alert (Owner: Maya Chen, due 2026-03-03)
- [ ] Add microbench regression asserts (Owner: Ethan Brooks, due 2026-03-10)
- [ ] Customer follow-up: CS to send timeline and credit note (Owner: Sofia Reyes, due 2026-03-01)

Notes & open questions:
- We should investigate whether similar kernel-selection thresholds exist elsewhere in the codebase that might impact other model families (V100, H100). (Action: cross-audit, owner: eng-serving-runtime)
- Consider adding synthetic traffic in preflight canaries to exercise memory-pressure and prefix reuse scenarios.
